title: Islamism and the Muslim Brotherhood
summary: In 1928 Hasan al-Banna, a schoolteacher in Ismailia, where the Suez Canal kept a large British presence, founded the Society of the Muslim Brothers to resist British imperial influence through renewed adherence to Islamic law. It ran clinics, schools and welfare for the poor, spread to Syria in the 1930s and became a political party in Egypt in 1939. Al-Banna was shot dead in 1949. After an attempt on Nasser's life in 1954 thousands were jailed, among them Sayyid Qutb, whose ideas inspired radical splinter groups.

beats.caption: In 1928, Hasan al-Banna founded the Muslim Brotherhood in Ismailia, Egypt, combining social welfare with religious revivalism.
The Brotherhood expanded across Egypt and neighboring Arab states, establishing the ideological blueprint for modern political Islam.
